audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 reads Skill while the mirror and the packet both give it to Fiora, and both item rows read Fiora while the mirror and packet give them to Sylas.
audit.why: Level 1 Sylas has one ability and no way to punish her Q-vital spacing, and by Riftmaker the omnivamp plus a stolen Grand Challenge makes him the better side-laner — the entry's own phases[5].why and phases[6].why already say so.
audit.corrected: Level 1 reads Fiora at 4/10; First item and Two+ items read Sylas at 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whys array is off by one from Level 6 onward: whys[4] (the Level 6 row) talks about Q-dash skirmish execution, while whys[5] (the First item row) opens with 'Hijack gives you Grand Challenge' — a level-6 event described one row too late.
audit.why: The reader gets the Hijack spike attached to the wrong timing, and the level-6 row says nothing about the ultimate at all.
audit.corrected: whys[4] rewritten as the level-6 Hijack row with Grand Challenge's 110s against your 80s; whys[5] rewritten as the Riftmaker row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte is described in four places as parrying damage and CC 'then stuns', unconditionally. Riot's text stabs for a SLOW, and stuns only if the parry blocked an immobilizing effect. Its 16-24s cooldown is also never stated.
audit.why: The conditional is the whole skill expression of the matchup: if nothing immobilising goes into the parry, the return is a slow you can walk out of, not a stun that kills you. Writing it as an automatic stun makes the player decline windows that are actually safe.
audit.corrected: Riposte restated as parry-into-slow, stunning only when it eats an immobilise, with the 16-24s cooldown attached.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds appears nowhere in the content layer despite Duelist's Dance healing her on every vital and Grand Challenge healing her and her allies.
audit.why: Her sustain is what makes the extended trade unwinnable; anti-heal timing is the purchase that changes it. On-hit is the second gap — Lunge applies on-hit effects, so armour alone reads the trade wrong.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named in whys[3] and the mid text; Lunge's on-hit application named in spikes[3].

edits.before: - Fiora Riposte: matchup-defining — Parries your damage and CC, then stuns — never lead with CC into it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E1 shield for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Fiora Riposte: matchup-defining — 16-24s. It parries everything, then slows; it only stuns if it ate an immobilise. - Grand Challenge is 110s against your 80s Hijack. - Grievous Wounds answers her vital healing.

edits.before: Parries your damage and CC, then stuns — never lead with CC into it. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Parries everything, then slows — it stuns only if it ate an immobilise. Bait it, count 16-24s, then go.

edits.before: Track Fiora’s Riposte: Parries your damage and CC, then stuns — never lead with CC into it. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Fiora’s Riposte: a 16-24s parry that answers with a slow, or a stun if it blocked an immobilise. Steps wait for its downtime.

edits.before: E is online but Riposte parries your E2 chain or W lunge and stuns you back — Fiora dictates every trade unless you bait the parry first.
edits.after: E is online but Riposte parries your chain or W lunge outright and slows you off — Fiora dictates every trade unless you bait the 24s parry first.

edits.before: Neither kit fully controls the window — your W heal can match her poke output but her vital procs off Q-spacing trade more efficiently than your chain combos without Riposte down.
edits.after: Neither kit fully controls the window — W can match her output, but every vital she hits heals her back, so without Grievous Wounds her Q-spacing simply trades more efficiently than your chain.

edits.before: You have E2 threat and passive autos but she Q-dashes in and out of vital range before your chain arrives — execution decides every skirmish here.
edits.after: Hijack takes Grand Challenge — her 110s ultimate on your 80s clock, and your copy reveals vitals on HER. Steal it the moment it is up.

edits.before: Hijack gives you Grand Challenge: she loses her R, you gain a copy that procs vitals on her, and your W heal turns all-ins winnable while Riposte is on cooldown.
edits.after: Riftmaker's omnivamp on top of the W heal finally matches her vital sustain, and a stolen Grand Challenge means the all-in is winnable whenever Riposte is on cooldown.

edits.before: Fiora's Q-AA-vital pattern beats your poke-in approach — she trades more efficiently through this window unless Riposte is clearly on cooldown.
edits.after: Fiora's Lunge applies on-hit and sets up the vital-auto pattern — she trades more efficiently here unless Riposte is clearly on cooldown.

edits.before: Land Riposte on your E2 stun or W lunge to negate your damage burst and stun you back
edits.after: Catch your chain or W lunge in Riposte, erasing the burst and slowing you out of range

edits.before: At level 1 you only have Q or W — do not step up for trades. Farm with Q tip and accept chip damage; forcing anything before E is online loses you HP you cannot afford to give a Fiora. At level 2 E arrives but Fiora's Riposte is already set to punish your first hook: she will parry the E2 chain or your W lunge, proc the stun back onto you, and cash a vital with you stunned. Spend levels 1-3 probing with Q poke and passive-empowered autos on her walk-ups, not committing the E while Riposte is healthy. Your only real pre-6 trade window opens when you see Riposte burn on a minion or a dodge attempt — then E2-Q-W immediately before it recharges.
edits.after: At level 1 you only have Q or W — do not step up for trades. Farm with Q tip and accept chip damage; forcing anything before E is online loses you HP you cannot afford to give a Fiora. At level 2 E arrives but Riposte is already set to punish your first hook: she parries the chain or your W lunge outright, slows you as she steps out, and cashes a vital while you walk. Spend levels 1-3 probing with Q poke and Petricite autos on her walk-ups, not committing E while Riposte is healthy. Your real pre-6 window opens when Riposte burns on a minion or a dodge — then E2-Q-W inside its 16-24s recharge.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a toss-up of execution. Her Q-dash spacing lets her walk into a vital, auto it, and step back before your chain arrives; your job is to threaten E2 as a fake to bait that backward step, then Q her in retreat and weave passive autos. Do not brawl into a full-HP Fiora with Riposte up — the percent-max-HP true damage from two or three vital procs will out-pace your W heal. At 6 the matchup pivots: steal Grand Challenge immediately, even if you're not all-inning yet. Now she has no R and you hold a copy that can proc vitals on her. Force the fight on her Riposte cooldown, lead with E1's shield to eat her burst, then chain E2 for the stun and burn W at low HP for the amplified heal.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a toss-up of execution. Lunge lets her step into a vital, auto it with on-hit applied, and leave before your chain arrives; threaten E2 as a fake to bait that step back, then Q her retreat and weave Petricite autos. Do not brawl a full-HP Fiora with Riposte up, and buy Grievous Wounds before you try — every vital she hits heals her through the exchange, and her Bladework second hit crits. At 6 the matchup pivots: steal Grand Challenge immediately, even if you are not fighting yet, because her 110s copy is gone while yours is back in 80. Force the fight inside Riposte's 16-24s gap, close with E1, recast to pull, and spend W at low HP for the bigger heal.

edits.before: With Riftmaker and a stolen Grand Challenge you become the teamfight threat Fiora never expected — your copy of her R can proc vitals on her in a side-lane duel, and the omnivamp keeps you alive through her true damage. In side-lane, never 1v1 her at two items if she's ahead: her vital damage scales with your max HP and your healing cannot keep pace with true damage. Play for river skirmishes and objectives instead, where stolen ultimates from other members of the enemy team may be stronger than her own R anyway. Your win condition is snowballing the 6-spike into a kill or Rift Herald control so the game ends before her two-item dueling peak fully arrives.
edits.after: With Riftmaker and a stolen Grand Challenge you become the teamfight threat Fiora never expected — your copy reveals vitals on her in a side-lane duel, and the omnivamp keeps you alive through her true damage. Never 1v1 her at two items if she is ahead: vital damage scales with your max HP and no resistance touches it, so only Grievous Wounds and clean spacing help you there. Play river skirmishes and objectives instead, where another enemy ultimate is often the better steal anyway. Your win condition is turning the 6-spike into a kill or Herald control before her two-item duelling peak fully arrives and the side lane closes.

notes: Riposte was written as an unconditional parry-into-stun in four places. Riot's text stabs for a slow and only stuns if the parry blocked an immobilizing effect — the conditional is the difference between 'never commit' and 'commit, just do not feed it CC'. Consistent with the mirror's abstention, I did not assert anything about whether Sylas's own E counts as an immobilise; the rewritten lines state Riposte's rule and let the reader apply it. The whys array was also off by one from Level 6 on, putting the Hijack spike in the first-item row; whys[4] and whys[5] are both rewritten to sit on their own rows.
